facts.rate: Social Security tax, employee share: 6.2% (statutory; employers pay a matching 6.2% to the same cap); Medicare 1.45% has no cap and is not counted
facts.wage_base: 2026: $184,500 (SSA '2026 Social Security Changes' fact sheet, released with the 2026 COLA in October 2025; Kiplinger)
facts.row_2: $184,500 × 6.2% = $11,439, the most anyone's wages pay in 2026
facts.verdict: You pay 6.2%. A $1M salary pays ≈ 1.1%. VO: 'You pay more than five times their rate' (6.2 ÷ 1.1439 = 5.42; 5.64 on the shown 1.1%)
facts.pinned: in dollars the $1M salary pays 4.4× the $20/hr worker ($11,439 ÷ $2,579.20 = 4.44) on 24× the pay ($1,000,000 ÷ $41,600 = 24.04); pay above the cap does not count toward benefits either (SSA: 'contribution and benefit base')
facts.not_modelled: self-employment tax (12.4% to the same cap), the employer's share, Medicare and its 0.9% surtax, two jobs (each employer withholds to the cap; the excess is refunded at tax time)

youtube.title_pick: You Pay 6.2% Social Security. What Does a Million-Dollar Salary Pay?
youtube.description:
You pay 6.2% Social Security tax on every paycheck. What does a million-dollar salary pay? In 2026 the 6.2% stops at $184,500 of wages, so a $1M salary pays $11,439: about 1.1% of its pay. You pay more than five times their rate.

The math, shown:
• At $20 an hour, full time (40 hrs × 52 wks = 2,080 hours): $20 × 2,080 × 6.2% ≈ $2,579 a year. All $41,600 is under the 2026 cap of $184,500, so every dollar pays 6.2%.
• The flat-rate guess: $1,000,000 × 6.2% = $62,000. No.
• In 2026 it stops at $184,500 (the wage base): $184,500 × 6.2% = $11,439, the most anyone's wages pay.
• $11,439 ÷ $1,000,000 ≈ 1.1% of their pay.
• You: 6.2% on every dollar, all year. Them: about 1.1%. More than five times their rate.

Follow for the math behind your money — shown, not hand-waved. @envelopemath

Animation and original sound: The Back of the Envelope. 2026 Social Security tax, employee share: 6.2% of wages up to $184,500 (SSA, 2026 Social Security Changes; Kiplinger). Employers pay a matching 6.2% to the same cap. Medicare (1.45%, no cap) is not counted. Not modelled: self-employment tax, and a second job (each employer withholds to the cap; the excess comes back at tax time). Not financial advice.
#SocialSecurity #taxes #paycheck

cover.frame_by_content: The clean cover, frame 1: the header '3 DEAD SIMPLE NUMBERS / YOU PAY 6.2% TO SOCIAL SECURITY. / A $1M SALARY PAYS…?' ('6.2%' in red), the footer 'ASSUMES 40 hrs × 52 wks · 2026 rates / employee share, no Medicare', the input line 'Your pay $20/hr 40 hrs a week', 3 numbered ledges labelled 'Yours, a year / A $1M salary pays / Their rate' (the last two with empty sockets), ① active with its '$20' block, and the green stick figure holding the '× 2,080 × 6.2%' plate. No result: it asks and does not answer, like the title and the caption. The write-up names frame 1 as the Instagram cover. On any cut, use the opening frame, before the figure flips the plate. cover.frame_measured: On the shipped 14.5 s condensed cut, frame 0 (0.00 s) is that frame and the only still one: the complete hook caption 'At $20 an hour, you pay about' is already up (it holds no result), and from frame 1 (0.03 s) the figure dips to flip the plate (mean frame-to-frame luma change 1.57, 270×480 greyscale). On the 26.5 s pre-condense render frame 0 had no caption.
cover.crop: 3:4 = 1080×1440, the top 1440 rows (y 0 to 1440) of the 1080×1920 frame: the badge, the header, the footer, the input line, the 3 ledges, the figure and the floor line, with even margins above the badge and below the floor; it drops the empty floor below. A crop from y 60 (as on 01a) leaves 200 px of empty floor. A centred grid crop (y 240-1680) cuts the badge and leaves the header on the edge.
